beats: Polyphemus drinks three bowls, promises Nobody the last death as a guest-gift, and collapses.
Odysseus heats the stake until it glows and the chosen men drive it into the Cyclops's eye.
They twist it as blood and steam erupt; Polyphemus wakes with a roar and tears it free.
Other Cyclopes call from outside, but leave when he says Nobody is killing him.
Polyphemus gropes at the entrance while the men hide among the animals.

segments.caption: What ails you, Polyphemus, that you wake the deathless night with screaming — is some man stealing your flocks, or killing you by craft or force? If Nobody harms you, alone as you are, it is sickness sent by Zeus, and cannot be helped — pray to your father Poseidon.
